speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of fear and worry about the future with AI.
zh: 对 AI 的未来存在很多恐惧和担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about this idea that if you fall behind, you're going to become part of this permanent underclass.
zh: 我想谈谈这个观点:如果你落后了,你就会变成这个永久底层阶级的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a funny dark fantasy that we seem to have as Silicon Valley collectively.
zh: 这是我们硅谷集体似乎拥有的一个有趣的黑暗幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things have never been better by almost every measure.
zh: 以几乎任何标准衡量,现在都是有史以来最好的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a technology that really amplifies our agency, it kind of unbundles skill from desire.
zh: 这项技术真正放大了我们的主观能动性,它某种程度上把技能和欲望解绑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only can we dramatically drive productivity, we can dramatically drive ambition.
zh: 我们不仅能大幅提升生产力,还能大幅提升雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you get too ambitious?
zh: 雄心会过大吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a limit?
zh: 有限度吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: In the old days, three years ago, we would see a company, and if what they were trying to do was too ambitious we would not engage.
zh: 在过去,三年前,我们看到一家公司,如果他们想做的事情野心太大,我们就不会参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we're almost seeing the opposite problem.
zh: 今天,我们看到的问题几乎正好相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: An idea that's too small is not something that we want to engage with.
zh: 一个太小的想法反而不是我们想参与的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have this interesting take that company building more and more is going to become this kind of series of creating loops?
zh: 你有一个有趣的观点:创建公司这件事会越来越多地变成一种创建循环的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to see this sort of cascading set of everything from a loop per person to loops that can run large parts of the company.
zh: 我们会看到这样一套级联式的循环,从每人一个循环,到能运营公司大部分业务的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that said, I think humans are a critical ingredient.
zh: 话虽如此,我认为人类是一个关键的要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: The loop will help you climb to the local maxima, but then it plateaus.
zh: 循环会帮助你爬升到局部最大值,但随后就会进入平台期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need human intuition, you need somebody to actually help you land at the base of the next hill.
zh: 你需要人类的直觉,需要有人真正帮助你在下一座山脚下落地。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have this take that the big opportunity is this idea of, "Loop, make me happier."
zh: 我们有这样一个观点:最大的机会是这个想法,“循环,让我更快乐。”

speaker: Unknown
en: We believe that people want to be more productive, but they don't.
zh: 我们相信人们想变得更高效,但他们并不想。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think more people want to spend time than save time.
zh: 我认为想要花时间的人多过想要节省时间的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that the opportunity for this technology is the basics of consumer need.
zh: 所以,我认为这项技术的机会在于消费者需求的基本面。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we feel more connected, more loved?
zh: 我们如何感到更连通、更被爱?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we make progress?
zh: 我们如何取得进展?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we have fun?
zh: 我们如何获得乐趣?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's a model or a capability challenge, it's just a product design challenge.
zh: 我不认为这是一个模型或能力层面的挑战,它只是一个产品设计层面的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my guest is Anish Acharya.
zh: 今天,我的嘉宾是 Anish Acharya。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anish is general partner at a16z, where he focuses on consumer investing.
zh: Anish 是 a16z 的普通合伙人,专注于消费领域投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is one of the most insightful, thought-provoking, mind-expanding, in-the-weeds product investors I've met.
zh: 他是我在见过的投资人中最有洞察力、最发人深省、最拓宽思维、又深入产品细节的产品投资人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's been at a16z for over seven years now, and unlike a lot of VCs, and why I loved having Anish on the podcast is that he is a longtime product builder and founder.
zh: 他已经在 a16z 待了七年多,和很多 VC 不同的是——这也是我喜欢请 Anish 来播客的原因——他是一位长期的产品构建者和创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He founded a company called SocialDeck, which he sold to Google, and then ended up leading a number of efforts within Google.
zh: 他创立了一家叫 SocialDeck 的公司,卖给了 Google,之后在 Google 内部领导了多个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then he started a new company called Snowball, which he then again sold, this time to Credit Karma, where he moved to VP of product and then GM of the broader consumer product and the whole entire credit card business.
zh: 然后他创办了一家叫 Snowball 的新公司,之后又再次卖掉了,这次是卖给了 Credit Karma,他在那里先担任产品副总裁,然后担任更广泛的消费产品和整个信用卡业务部门的 GM。

speaker: Unknown
en: This conversation will get your mind buzzing.
zh: 这场对话会让你的头脑嗡嗡作响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get into it, don't forget to check out lennysproductpass.com for a free year of the hottest and most beautifully crafted AI products in the world available exclusively to Lenny's newsletter subscribers.
zh: 在我们开始之前,别忘了去 lennysproductpass.com 看看,那里有为期一年的免费世界上最热门、制作最精美的 AI 产品,专门提供给 Lenny's newsletter 的订阅者。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I bring you Anish Acharya.
zh: 那么,我为你们带来 Anish Acharya。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anish, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Anish,非常感谢你来到这里,欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, Lenny.
zh: 谢谢你,Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so excited to be here, thrilled.
zh: 我非常兴奋能来到这里,太开心了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with a very light topic.
zh: 我想从一个非常轻松的话题开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about this meme of the permanent underclass.
zh: 我想谈谈永久底层阶级这个梗。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of this joke that people half joke about, this idea that if you fall behind and aren't just on top of all the latest AI tools, aren't becoming the most productive person ever, you're going to become part of this permanent underclass and fall behind and have a really hard time.
zh: 这是人们半开玩笑地说的一个笑话,意思是如果你落后了,没有掌握所有最新的 AI 工具,没有成为有史以来最高效的人,你就会变成这个永久底层阶级的一员,落后于人,日子会非常难过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some people joke about it, I think a lot of people take this really seriously and stresses a lot of people out.
zh: 有些人拿它开玩笑,但我觉得很多人非常认真地对待这件事,这让很多人压力很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: How real of a concern do you think this really is?
zh: 你觉得这个担忧到底有多真实?

speaker: Unknown
en: How seriously do you think people should take this?
zh: 你觉得人们应该多认真地对待这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not very seriously, and it's a funny dark fantasy that we seem to have as Silicon Valley collectively.
zh: 不用太认真,这是我们硅谷集体似乎拥有的一个有趣的黑暗幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things have never been better, really by almost every measure, by how distributed all the opportunities are, by the kind of technology we have access to, to the types of ambition we're allowed to have, and to the number of companies that are independently working on things that are winning.
zh: 现在真的是有史以来最好的时代,以几乎任何标准衡量——机会分布的广泛程度、我们能接触到的技术类型、我们被允许拥有的雄心类型,以及独立做出成功事业的公司数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet there's this sort of discussion of permanent underclass, being outside of the light cone, I've heard it.
zh: 然而却有这种关于永久底层阶级的讨论,关于处于光锥之外的讨论,我听说过这种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just something for deep insiders or outsiders, it feels like there's a real fear from researchers at foundation model labs all the way through to the Silicon Valley layman.
zh: 而且这不仅仅是深度内部人士或圈外人士的话题,从基础模型实验室的研究人员到硅谷的普通人,似乎都存在一种真实的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, here's a couple of points that I think are really important.
zh: 我的意思是,有几点我认为非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, I think the last era of tech was a lot more centralized.
zh: 首先,我认为上一个科技时代要中心化得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at network effects, that's sort of the gold standard.
zh: 如果你看网络效应,那算是黄金标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: You worked on a network effects product, that's the gold standard of businesses from the mobile era, and those things led to dramatic centralization.
zh: 你做一个网络效应产品,那是移动时代商业的黄金标准,而这些东西导致了戏剧性的中心化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, all of them are definitionally sort of N-of-1 networks.
zh: 当然,从定义上讲,它们都属于某种 N-of-1 网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at what's happening now, it's like every part of the stack there's not even two relevant players, there's 20.
zh: 如果你看看现在正在发生的事,在技术栈的每一个部分,都不止两个相关玩家,而是有二十个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got labs, you've got open weight, you've got different variations within both.
zh: 有实验室,有开放权重模型,两者内部还有各种不同的变体。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at coding agents, we were talking about it, your mental model for two years ago should have been, would've been, I think it should be winner take all, and yet Claude Code, Codex, Lovable, Replit, Wabi, they're all sort of working.
zh: 如果你看编程智能体这个领域,我们之前聊过,你两年前的心智模型应该是——我想它应该是——赢家通吃,然而 Claude Code、Codex、Lovable、Replit、Wabi,它们全都在某种程度上运转着。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really, really encouraging to see that.
zh: 所以看到这一点真的、真的令人鼓舞。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing, you've heard all the kind of economic data, everything from radiologists who are supposed to be cooked every year for I think about 20 years now.
zh: 第二件事,你已经听过各种经济数据了,比如放射科医生,他们被认为每年都要完蛋,我想到现在已经差不多二十年了吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, job postings are higher than they've ever been, as well as programmers.
zh: 而当然,职位招聘数量比以往任何时候都高,程序员也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I don't know that the empirical data bears it out.
zh: 所以,我不认为经验数据支持那种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the final thing is that there's this sort of discussion about RSI, and I know RSI is like recursive self-improvement is a fun term to throw around, but if you ask the most sophisticated individuals at the labs, it's not actually RSI that's occurring, which could lead to some sort of runaway winner because they were an epsilon ahead of the others.
zh: 我想最后一点是,关于 RSI 有这么一种讨论,我知道 RSI 也就是递归自我改进,是个拿来炒作很有趣的词,但如果你去问实验室里最顶尖的那些人,实际发生的并不是真正的 RSI——那才可能导致某种失控的赢家,因为他们只是比其他人领先了一个 epsilon。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's auto catalytic effects, which just means you're using the technology to improve your process, but it's not truly recursive.
zh: 实际发生的是自催化效应,这只是意味着你在用这项技术来改进你的流程,但它并不是真正递归的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think everything from the most empirical to the most technical view points in the other direction, and yet we can't seem to let go of this fantasy.
zh: 所以,我认为从最经验性的到最技术性的观点,一切都指向相反的方向,然而我们似乎就是无法放下这个幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something I've been thinking about recently, even seeing these crazy stories about OpenAI's models hacking Hugging Face, all these stories to me feels like there's always been this question of are we on the fast takeoff or the slow takeoff scenario?
zh: 最近我一直在想一件事,甚至看到那些关于 OpenAI 的模型入侵 Hugging Face 的疯狂报道,所有这些故事让我觉得,一直都有这样一个问题:我们是在快速起飞还是慢速起飞的场景里?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels very much so that we are on the slow takeoff scenario, because every one of these milestones it's like, "Holy shit, it hacked ..." We had no idea it was doing this, but we're catching it, we're watching it, we're observing it, we're iterating, evolving.
zh: 而现在感觉非常明显,我们处于慢速起飞的场景,因为每一个里程碑发生时都是这样的:“我的天,它入侵了……”我们完全不知道它在做这件事,但我们在捕获它,我们在观察它,我们在监测它,我们在迭代、演化。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always this fear, "Okay, but tomorrow it's going to take off."
zh: 总是有这种恐惧:“好吧,但明天它就要起飞了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm hearing from you is that's probably not the case, which I think is the source of a lot of people's fears, this idea that all of a sudden it's going to become super, super intelligent and then we're in big trouble.
zh: 我从你这里听到的是,情况可能并非如此,我认为这正是很多人恐惧的来源——这种想法:突然之间它会变得超级、超级智能,然后我们就麻烦大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: The line of reasoning for that case is always everything up until now, then something happens that no one can quite articulate and then fast take off.
zh: 这种论点的推理线永远是:到今天为止的一切,然后发生了某种没人能说清楚的事情,然后就是快速起飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I don't believe that that's going to happen.
zh: 所以,我不相信那种事会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that model progress is happening faster than ever before, but if you look at something like economic diffusion, I grew up in a small town, I went back home last summer, people's lives haven't changed that much.
zh: 我确实认为模型进步正在以前所未有的速度发生,但如果你看看经济扩散这类事情,我在一个小镇长大,去年夏天我回了一趟老家,人们的生活并没有那么大的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if nothing else, the sort of slow rate of economic diffusion will catch it.
zh: 所以退一万步说,经济扩散的缓慢速度也会把它兜住。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the other thing that's under discussed, Lenny, is how many problems are truly intelligence bound?
zh: 我认为另一件被讨论得不够的事,Lenny,是有多少问题真正是受智能约束的?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had a data center of PhDs working at FedEx or Domino's Pizza, are they going to be exponentially dominating supply chain and pizzas?
zh: 如果你让一群 PhD 组成的数据中心去 FedEx 或达美乐披萨工作,他们会指数级地主导供应链和披萨吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think we might be overestimating how many problems are intelligence bound versus bound by other things.
zh: 所以,我想我们可能高估了有多少问题是受智能约束的,而不是被其他东西约束的。

en: What are you seeing inside of companies in terms of is there more of a divide happening and do you think there will be more of a divide between the people that are becoming really good and embracing versus like, "I don't have time for this, I hate all this stuff, my job's already so stressful"?
zh: 你在公司内部看到的是什么情况——是不是正在出现更多的分化,你认为在那些正在变得非常擅长并拥抱这些工具的人,和那些“我没时间搞这个,我讨厌这些东西,我的工作已经够有压力了”的人之间,会有更大的分化吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you seeing happening and where do you think things will go inside of companies in terms of maybe a divide?
zh: 你看到了什么正在发生,你认为公司内部在可能的分化方面,事情会往什么方向发展?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I have so many thoughts on this.
zh: 这个嘛,我对此有非常多的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we give the average employee enough credit.
zh: 我不认为我们对普通员工有足够的信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we have this abstraction of a white collar employee.
zh: 我认为我们对白领员工有一种抽象化的想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: The white collar manager, the abstraction is like some Dilbert-esque manager who's just shuffling paper all day long.
zh: 白领经理,这个抽象形象就像某个呆伯特式的经理,整天只是来回搬弄文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have this abstraction of consumers that they're sort of these low agency NPCs.
zh: 我们对消费者也有一种抽象想象,觉得他们是某种低主观能动性的 NPC。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, that would never apply to us or our friends.
zh: 当然,这种想象永远不会适用于我们自己或我们的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have this abstraction that everybody else's job is super automatable by AI, but of course ours is not.
zh: 我们有一种抽象想象,觉得所有人的工作都超级容易被 AI 自动化,但当然我们自己的工作不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think when you actually get into the details, a lot of people are actually excited to better themselves, get more leverage.
zh: 所以,我认为当你真正深入细节时,很多人其实是很兴奋去提升自己、获得更多杠杆的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you see this with, of course, sophisticated companies like Google, but even a company like Kavak where they sell used cars in Mexico, they've got this concept of a Jedi academy where they're teaching everybody at the company, including the mechanics, how to use the new tools and technologies and at the end of the six-week course they ship a cutting edge in-production agent.
zh: 你可以在像 Google 这样成熟的公司看到这一点,但甚至像 Kavak 这样在墨西哥卖二手车的公司,他们有一个叫绝地学院的概念,他们在教公司里的每一个人,包括机械师,如何使用新的工具和技术,在这个为期六周的课程结束时,他们会交付一个尖端的、在生产环境中运行的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I actually think that more people are embracing the technology than we sort of like to discuss.
zh: 所以,我实际上认为,拥抱这项技术的人比我们乐于讨论的要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a big change is going to be using AI versus reorganizing your entire company around AI.
zh: 我认为一个重大变化将是:使用 AI, versus 围绕 AI 重组你的整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a great example of this is if you look at the diffusion of electricity as a technology, it took 40 years for us to get from the inception of electricity to reorganizing factories.
zh: 一个很好的例子是,如果你看看电力作为一项技术的扩散,从电力的诞生到重组工厂,我们花了四十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means burning the buildings down and starting from scratch versus taking what was previously coal and simply swapping it with electricity.

en: I think a useful way to think about it is anytime the model's making a mistake or doing something you wouldn't do, what do you know that it doesn't know?
zh: 我认为一个有用的思考方式是，每当模型犯错或做了你不会做的事，问问自己：你知道什么而它不知道？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a really interesting example I heard from Ale at Kavak.
zh: 我从 Kavak 的 Ale 那里听到过一个非常有意思的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's probably the most sophisticated thinker on this stuff that I get to hang out with, where he said anytime their agent, they have an agent per customer, they sell used cars online, and when the agent gets stuck it actually calls a human, and the human will coach the agent through.
zh: 他可能是我在这个问题上能接触到的最深刻的思考者，他说每当他们的智能体——他们每个客户有一个智能体，他们在线销售二手车——当智能体卡住的时候，它实际上会打给一个人，而那个人会指导智能体度过难关。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the magic of that is not only does it unblock the agent, but of course the agent then captures all the traces and learns from it.
zh: 这其中的神奇之处在于，它不仅解除了智能体的阻塞，而且当然智能体随后会捕获所有的轨迹并从中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really interesting mental model.
zh: 这是一个非常有意思的心智模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's either a knowledge gap or a data gap that you have to give the agent, and the next time it shouldn't have to call you.
zh: 这是你要给智能体补上的一个知识缺口或数据缺口，这样下次它就不必再打给你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that example.
zh: 我喜欢这个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, the takeaway here is you need to start thinking about every function as an agent loop, and the job is to figure out where it gets blocked, where it goes wrong, and give it more context, more insight, more direction, basically.
zh: 基本上，这里的要点是，你需要开始把每个职能都视为一个智能体循环，而你的工作就是找出它在哪里被阻塞、哪里出了问题，然后基本上给它更多的上下文、更多的洞察、更多的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's right.
zh: 是的，就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then hopefully a lot of your day-to-day work, when you come up with a new idea that works, the kind of implications of that idea, if it's a product, there's marketing work, there's sales work, there's product marketing, there's communication, there's legal, all of that should be largely handled for you.
zh: 然后但愿你很多日常工作，当你想出一个有效的新想法时，这个想法的各种衍生影响，如果它是一个产品，就有营销工作、销售工作、产品营销、传播、法务，所有这些都应该在很大程度上替你处理好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your job is to go take a hike and dream the dreams and come up with the next hill to climb.
zh: 而你的工作就是去远足、做梦，想出下一个要攀登的山头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this begs the question a bit of just what will separate the companies that win in this world where AI is kind of doing a lot of this?
zh: 这就引出了一个问题：在 AI 承担了很多这类工作的世界里，什么将把赢家公司区分出来？

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine part of the answer is the human in this local maxima coming in with a better idea.
zh: 我想象答案的一部分是，处于这些局部最优中的人带着更好的想法进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else that you think becomes a differentiator in this world where AI is doing so much of the work that humans are currently doing?
zh: 在这个 AI 承担了人类目前所做的这么多工作的世界里，你认为还有什么会成为差异化因素吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think one thing that's under discussed is that it's unclear that the sort of competitive equilibria that exists in a lot of industries will really change.
zh: 我是说，我认为有一个被讨论不足的事情是，很多行业中存在的那种竞争格局是否真的会改变，这一点并不明确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let's say Pizza Hut, and Domino's, and Papa John's, and Roundtable all get a data center of PhDs, and they're all going to either adopt it or have a CEO change and adopt it.
zh: 所以，假设必胜客、达美乐、棒约翰和 Roundtable 都得到了一个由博士组成的数据中心，它们要么会采用它，要么换一个 CEO 然后采用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it'll be a rocky period and there'll be some relative shuffling, but I think that they're all going to embrace the new technology because most companies do.
zh: 所以，会有一段颠簸的时期，也会有一些相对的洗牌，但我认为它们都会拥抱新技术，因为大多数公司都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know that one of them is going to have 99% of the market.
zh: 我不认为其中一家会占有 99% 的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think what's under discussed is that yes, in the near term I think there'll be winners and losers based on adoption of the technology and how ambitiously you adopt it.
zh: 所以，我认为被讨论不足的一点是，是的，短期内我认为会基于技术的采用、以及你采用它时有多激进，而产生赢家和输家。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think there's a lot of industries that will sort of maintain their current competitive dynamics because they're not intelligence bound.
zh: 但我确实认为有很多行业会大致维持它们目前的竞争格局，因为它们不受智能的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the most useful question to ask yourself as a founder CEO is just, "Hey, if we assume these things are infinitely intelligent and astonishingly cheap, how would we reorganize the company?"
zh: 我认为作为一个创始人 CEO，最值得问自己的问题就是：“嘿，如果我们假设这些东西拥有无限的智能、而且便宜得惊人，我们会如何重组这家公司？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's where we're going?
zh: 因为那正是我们要去的方向？

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of along those lines, you have this interesting take about this kind of split that might be coming within companies between these generalists and specialists, and how AI plays into that.
zh: 顺着这个思路，你有一个有趣的观点，关于公司内部可能在通才和专才之间出现的这种分裂，以及 AI 如何参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about that.
zh: 谈谈这个吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think that there's so many interesting things that this touches on.
zh: 嗯，我认为这触及了很多有趣的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the question of open weight versus frontier.
zh: 一个是开放权重与前沿模型的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm sure, are you familiar with Pareto efficiency?
zh: 那么，我确信，你熟悉帕累托效率吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure you are.
zh: 你肯定熟悉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Please explain.
zh: 请解释一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so Pareto efficiency is just for price performance, for example, the efficient frontier is what's considered the optimal trade-off of a unit of performance for a unit of price.
zh: 好，帕累托效率就是，比如说对于性价比，有效前沿被认为是用一单位价格换取一单位性能的最优权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're along that curve, you're always paying the rational amount for the performance.
zh: 如果你处在那条曲线上，你为性能支付的就总是理性金额。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's interesting is that frontier models are actually irrationally priced in that, first of all, Mythos is infinite dollars a token, you can't use it.
zh: 而有意思的是，前沿模型实际上定价是非理性的，首先，Mythos 是每 token 无限美元，你根本没法用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you look at even something like Fable 5, for one IQ, conceptually one IQ of extra intelligence you're paying 100X more than Opus 4.8.
zh: 但即使看像 Fable 5 这样的东西，概念上每多一个 IQ 的额外智能，你支付的价格是 Opus 4.8 的 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not rational, but I think there's a lot of jobs in which you have unbounded upside, like drug discovery.
zh: 所以这不理性，但我认为有很多工作其上行空间是无界的，比如药物发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that one IQ point lets you discover the next statin, it's a trillion dollar outcome.
zh: 如果那一个 IQ 点让你发现了下一款他汀类药物，那就是万亿美元级的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it's sort of rational to pay for the highest intelligence in these types of jobs and industries.
zh: 所以，在这类工作和行业里，为最高的智能付费是某种程度上的理性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now on the other hand, I'm going to pick on maybe legal.
zh: 另一方面，我来拿法律行业开刀吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's perhaps only so much upside to be had in legal or finance.
zh: 法律或金融领域也许只有那么多的上行空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for those jobs, you actually do want to be very Pareto efficient and probably pay for good performance at a good price, not infinitely priced, infinite potential upside performance.
zh: 对于那些工作，你实际上确实想要非常帕累托高效，可能为好的性能支付好的价格，而不是为无限定价的、有无限潜在上行空间的性能买单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think what we're going to see is a split between job functions that demand kind of mid-IQ intelligence, and those will often be open weight, sort of biased with reinforcement learning, things that make the models even cheaper, more performant for a narrow job, along with incredibly "expensive but performant" frontier tokens for sales, support, research, engineering.
zh: 所以，我认为我们将看到的是一种分裂：一类工作职能只需要中等 IQ 的智能，它们往往是开放权重、通过强化学习偏置调整的，让模型对某个狭窄的工作更便宜、更高效；另一类则是令人难以置信的“昂贵但高效”的前沿 token，用于销售、支持、研究、工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think you're going to end up having both architectures, and we can touch on this in a little bit but I do think there are these sort of comparative advantages amongst model families, and then also amongst, of course, individual models that we're seeing more and more of.
zh: 所以，我认为你最终会同时拥有这两种架构，我们可以稍后再深入这个话题，但我确实认为模型家族之间存在这些比较优势，当然，在各个单独的模型之间也存在，而且我们看到的越来越多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not going to be one or the other.
zh: 这不会是非此即彼的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Such an interesting insight.
zh: 这么有意思的洞察。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, just to make sure I understand what you're describing here, you're thinking there's going to be this split between within an org of function and model, where specific functions that have a lot more upside and potential leverage go for the frontier models, and you described these kind of product sales, engineering research roles.
zh: 那么，为了确认我理解你所描述的内容，你的意思是，在一个组织内部会按职能和模型出现一种分化，那些上升空间更大、潜在杠杆更高的职能会用前沿模型，你描述的这类产品、销售、工程研究岗位就是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, for other functions you don't need Mythos, you don't need Astra, I think is that the latest one that's coming?
zh: 然后，对于其他职能，你不需要 Mythos,也不需要 Astra——我想这是即将推出的最新那个？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, Astra.
zh: 是的，Astra。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 对，对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's both, you're saying the AI doesn't need to be the frontier model and the people don't have to be the smartest people in the world to do really well in that world.
zh: 所以你说的就是，AI 不必是前沿模型，人也不必是世界上最聪明的人，在那个世界里也能做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I don't want to be diminutive.
zh: 是的，我不想显得贬低。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's extraordinary people in those job functions.
zh: 那些岗位职能里有非常出色的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think that they're bounded upside problems that they work on.
zh: 我只是认为，他们所处理的问题的上升空间是有边界的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can only kind of close the books correctly, you can't close the books 100X better.
zh: 你只能把账目正确地结清，你没法把账结得好上 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, that's exactly what I'm saying.
zh: 所以是的，这就是我要说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder if it's connected back to that discussion we had earlier about it's verifiable.
zh: 我想知道这是否和我们之前那次讨论有关联，就是关于它是可验证的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's a lot more verifiable, you don't need the frontier model versus, I don't know, the potential upside.
zh: 如果一个问题的可验证性强得多，你就不需要前沿模型，而不像，我不知道，潜在的上升空间那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure.
zh: 我不确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think for a ... Verifiability is a good question because I think for a drug development company, you have infinite upside, it is verifiable, but closing the books is also a verifiable problem, which has limited upside.
zh: 我是说，我觉得对于……可验证性是个好问题，因为对于一家药物研发公司来说，上升空间是无限的，而且它是可验证的，但结账也是一个可验证的问题，但上升空间有限。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the question is really how much upside is there and how hard is it to calculate it?
zh: 我认为真正的问题是，上升空间有多大，以及计算它有多难？

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a nuance.
zh: 这里有个细微之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Customer support, a customer may call in and report a bug.
zh: 客户支持，一个客户可能打进来报告一个 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: That bug may actually be the first breadcrumb to a thing that changes our entire organization.
zh: 那个 bug 可能实际上是一个线索的开端，能引出改变我们整个组织的某种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the CEO was on that call or the smartest person, they could follow the trail.
zh: 如果是 CEO 或者最聪明的人在那个电话上，他们可以顺着线索追下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we actually have this "mid-IQ generalist," then not, that actually makes the case for as a basket of problems always use frontier intelligence.
zh: 但如果我们真的用这种“中等智商的通才”，那就抓不到了，这实际上支持了一个论点：作为一个问题集合，总是要用前沿智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can of course make the case for the mid-IQ basket as well, which is simply that we've crossed an intelligence threshold for almost every economically useful problem, and anything beyond that threshold is simply waste.
zh: 当然我也可以为中等智商集合辩护，理由很简单：对于几乎每一个经济上有用的问题，我们已经跨过了智能阈值，超过那个阈值的任何东西都只是浪费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the point people forget is that the models that are not the frontier models, that was what the frontier was, I don't know, six months ago, and we were so impressed and we loved it.
zh: 而且我认为人们忘记的一点是，那些不是前沿模型的模型，那可是，我不知道，六个月前的前沿，我们当时那么惊叹，我们那么喜爱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, "Holy shit, it can do all this."
zh: 当时就像是，“我去，它居然能做这一切。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And now just because there's something better, we don't give those models as much credit.
zh: 而现在仅仅因为有了更好的东西，我们就不再给那些模型那么多认可了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're right, because it's sort of like, "This thing is so crazy.
zh: 你说得对，因为这有点像是，“这个东西太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is AGI."
zh: 这就是 AGI。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, a day later it's like the old thing that you throw in the dustbin.
zh: 然后，一天之后它就成了你扔进垃圾堆的旧东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So along those lines, I hear people jokingly call you a model sommelier.
zh: 沿着这个思路，我听到有人开玩笑地称你为模型侍酒师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us with your sommelier credentials, what's the current state of the model art?
zh: 以你的侍酒师资历，告诉我们模型艺术的现状吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is each model great at?
zh: 每个模型各自擅长什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are model's terrible at?
zh: 每个(各个)模型糟糕在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, as you know, the secret of every sommelier is 10,000 hours or maybe 10,000 bottles.
zh: 嗯，如你所知，每个侍酒师的秘诀是一万小时，或者也许是一万瓶酒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that the secret of being a model sommelier is just using them all.
zh: 所以，我认为成为模型侍酒师的秘诀就是把它们全都用一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Drinking them all.
zh: 把它们全都“喝”一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I push myself really hard to ship something with every new model that comes out, and I think you learn so much.
zh: 我非常用力地推动自己，每当有新模型发布就用它交付点什么，我觉得你能学到非常多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for people who believe the models are commodities or totally fungible, you just haven't actually used the models.
zh: 我认为对于那些相信模型是大宗商品或完全可互换的人来说，你只是真的没有用过这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for example, in the last few weeks I've been obsessed with Qwen 3.8-Max.
zh: 举例来说，最近几周我一直痴迷于 Qwen 3.8-Max。

speaker: Unknown
en: Qwen is an awesome model.
zh: Qwen 是一个很棒的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very good at long horizon tasks, and it's actually really creative.
zh: 它非常擅长长时程任务，而且它真的很有创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great storyteller.
zh: 它是一个很棒的讲故事者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I've been using it to create these impossible documentaries, mostly of planets of the Star Wars universe.
zh: 所以我一直在用它创作这些不可能的纪录片，主要是星球大战宇宙中的行星。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did Tataouine, which turned out great.
zh: 我做了塔图因，结果很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did Bespin last night, and it can just work for four or five hours.
zh: 我昨晚做了贝斯坪，它能连续工作四五个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: It tells a great story, it generates all the video using the MiniMax model via Fal, generates audio via Eleven.
zh: 它讲了一个很棒的故事，它通过 Fal 使用 MiniMax 模型生成所有视频，通过 Eleven 生成音频。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually directs the movie, the five-minute movie, and then it cuts all of the clips in.
zh: 它实际上在导演这部电影，这部五分钟的电影，然后它把所有片段剪辑进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It overlays it, it watches it.
zh: 它叠加、它观看。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just extraordinary.
zh: 真是 extraordinary,非常非凡。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got a totally different shape than GLM-5.2.
zh: 它的形态和 GLM-5.2 完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: GLM-5.3 just came out, which I used for a bunch of product work.
zh: GLM-5.3 刚刚发布，我用它做了一堆产品工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't have a vision component, and it's sort of like this neurotic PhD you put in the corner, and they both have the role.
zh: 它没有视觉组件，它有点像你放在角落里的神经质的博士，而它们都有各自的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a little bit of these tension of models.
zh: 这是模型之间的一点张力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that one is ahead of another, one is more intelligent, it's rather one has a mind that's shaped in one direction, perhaps creativity and openness for Qwen, and others that are shaped in other directions like neuroticism and precision like GLM-5.3.
zh: 并不是说谁领先于谁，谁更智能，而是一个模型的心智朝一个方向塑造，比如 Qwen 的创造性和开放性，而其他的朝别的方向塑造，比如神经质和精确性，像 GLM-5.3。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I just make something with every model and that's how I build my intuition.
zh: 所以，我用每个模型都做点东西，这就是我建立直觉的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: How important is this habit, do you think, for people?
zh: 你觉得这个习惯对人们来说有多重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I hear a lot that it's really important to be using these models.
zh: 因为我经常听到说使用这些模型真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a secondary question is how do you come up with what to do with these models?
zh: 第二个问题是你怎么想出用这些模型做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because a lot of people want to try these things.
zh: 因为很多人都想试试这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, "Okay, what do I do?"
zh: 他们会说：“好吧，我该做什么？”

speaker: Anish Acharya
en: I know.
zh: 我知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any suggestions?
zh: 有什么建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think almost all of us have got ...
zh: 嗯，我觉得我们几乎所有人都有……

en: The most insufferable thing for a long time was your app idea friend.
zh: 长期以来最让人受不了的就是你那个有 app 创意的朋友。

en: Every time you went to have a beer they're like, "Let me tell you my app idea."
zh: 每次你去喝啤酒，他们就说：“让我告诉你我的 app 创意。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, "Oh, here we go again."
zh: 你会说：“哦，又来了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: We have got to be the app idea guys now, and all the silly ideas, actually, especially the silly ideas, because those are the ones that often have the most alpha, are the ones that we should all be building.
zh: 我们现在都得成为那种有 app 创意的人，所有那些傻主意，实际上，尤其是那些傻主意，因为那些往往是 alpha 最多的，正是我们都应该去构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I've probably got two dozen apps that I've built, I've got one or two large apps that I iterate on.
zh: 所以，我大概已经构建了两打 app，其中有一两个大的 app 我在持续迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that if you don't have a chassis with which to use the models, it's just really hard to come up with an idea from scratch every time.
zh: 而且我觉得，如果你没有一个使用模型的载体，每次都从零开始想一个主意真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I'd say work on something.
zh: 所以，我会说去做点东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually better if it's not important with a capital I, and then keep finding new ways to invest in it and add to it with a model as a kind of tool rather than as a goal.
zh: 实际上，如果它不是大写 I 的重要(Important)的东西反而更好，然后不断寻找新的方式投入其中、用模型往里面添加东西，把模型当作一种工具而不是目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that make sense?
zh: 这样说得通吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe even zooming out, I've been thinking more and more one of the most important habits to build right now is to, whenever you're about to do something, ask yourself, "How can AI do this for me?"
zh: 也许再拉远一点说，我越来越多地在想，现在最该养成的习惯之一就是，每当你正要做某件事时，问自己：“AI 能怎么替我做这件事？”

speaker: Anish Acharya
en: Totally.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm visualizing this input to response, the whole idea of there's a space between input and response, and meditation helps you think more deeply before you respond.
zh: 我在想象这个输入到响应的过程，也就是在输入和响应之间存在一个空间，而冥想能帮助你在回应之前更深入地思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like the trick now is insert in that moment, "How can AI help me with this?"
zh: 我觉得现在的诀窍就是在那个时刻插入：“AI 能怎么帮我做这件事？”

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I'm also a longtime meditator.
zh: 我是说，我自己也是长期的冥想者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should talk about that if you like, but yeah, I think that's right.
zh: 如果你愿意我们可以聊聊那个，不过是的，我觉得你说得对。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in our day-to-day knowledge work, sometimes it's less obvious to me.
zh: 我觉得在我们的日常知识工作中，对我来说有时不那么明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess my mind is I've always been a consumer product person, I love products.
zh: 我想我的思路是，我一直是个消费产品的人，我热爱产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for me, it's easier to think of a new feature to add to my DJ streaming app or my Google Reader for X that I use than it is to find a part of my life to automate.
zh: 所以对我来说，想出一个可以加到我的 DJ 流媒体 app 或者我自用的 X 上的 Google Reader 里的新功能，比找到生活中一个可以自动化的部分更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're right, there's some fun examples.
zh: 但你说得对，也有一些好玩的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I posted about one a few weeks ago where I had my laptop transcribe everything that was happening in the kitchen, and then it would award or detract screen time from my son's iPad depending on whether he was being good or bad.
zh: 几周前我发过一个例子，我让我的笔记本电脑转录厨房里发生的一切，然后根据我儿子表现得好还是不好，给他的 iPad 增加或扣除屏幕时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it was a fun little social experiment.
zh: 所以，那是一个好玩的小社会实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also had a fun outcome, which is that he recorded a video of himself saying, "I love you, Dad," over and over, and put it next to the mic.
zh: 它还有一个好玩的结果，那就是他录了一段自己反复说“爸爸，我爱你”的视频，放在麦克风旁边。

speaker: Unknown
en: To hack the metrics?
zh: 为了黑掉指标？

speaker: Unknown
en: To hack the metrics.
zh: 为了黑掉指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yes, anything becomes a measure it's no longer useful, but it was just a cool little social experiment.
zh: 所以是的，任何东西一旦变成衡量指标就不再有用了，但那确实是一个很酷的小社会实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think those things are super fun.
zh: 我觉得这类东西特别好玩。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is hilarious.
zh: 那真是太搞笑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, one of the measures was how often he said, "I love you," and that was going to give him more free time?
zh: 所以，其中一个衡量指标是他多久说一次“我爱你”，那会给他更多自由时间？

speaker: Anish Acharya
en: Is he saying things that are positive and pro-social-
zh: 是他在说积极的、亲社会的话——

speaker: Unknown
en: That is so funny.
zh: 那太好笑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... or negative and antisocial?
zh: ……还是消极的、反社会的话？

speaker: Unknown
en: And saying, "I love you," is very pro-social.
zh: 而说“我爱你”是非常亲社会的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's so funny.
zh: 那太好笑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a friend who built this little device that measured how often he and his kid laugh throughout the day.
zh: 我有个朋友做了个小设备，测量他和他孩子一整天笑的次数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, that's nice.
zh: 哦，那真好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He hacked one of those Limitless pendants to do that, and then they just look at that metric every day.
zh: 他改装了一个 Limitless 挂坠来实现这个功能，然后他们每天都盯着那个指标看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is what I mean, man.
zh: 而这就是我说的意思，伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we spent a lot of the time on the show so far really intriguing, talking about productivity, job loss, all these heady, important topics with a capital I, but what you just described, how often you laugh, that's not a startup, that's probably not an economically consequential idea, but it is for the quality of our life.
zh: 我觉得我们这期节目到目前为止花了很多时间在讨论那些非常引人入胜、大写的「重要」话题——生产力、失业等等，但你刚才描述的东西——你笑的频率——那不是一个创业项目，可能也不是一个有经济影响力的想法，但它关系到我们生活的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we tend to think that happiness is fixed, but what if it's not?
zh: 而且我倾向于认为快乐是固定不变的，但如果它不是呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you and I were doing jobs 100 years ago, what would our jobs be?
zh: 如果你我是在 100 年前工作，我们的工作会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I promise they'd be less cool than they are right now, and maybe 100 years from now they'll be that much cooler.
zh: 我保证会比现在的工作没那么酷，而也许 100 年后会再酷那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that the thing that gets often missed, and this is why I'm a fan of Claire and others, is just how can this thing add texture to our human lives even if they don't have economic consequences?
zh: 所以，我觉得经常被忽略的一点——这也是为什么我是 Claire 和其他人的粉丝——就是这个东西如何能为我们的日常生活增添质感，哪怕它没有经济后果？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along these lines I saw somewhere you have this really interesting take that the big opportunity, maybe just in consumer, but broadly is this idea of, "Loop, make me happier."
zh: 沿着这个思路，我看到 somewhere 你有一个非常有意思的观点，认为最大的机会——也许只在消费领域，但也可以更广泛——就是「Loop，让我更快乐」这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about that.
zh: 聊聊这个吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah.
zh: 哦，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think that we believe that people want to be more productive, but they don't.
zh: 我是说，我们相信人们想要更有生产力，但他们其实不想。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think more people want to spend time than save time.
zh: 我认为想要花时间的人多于想要省时间的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a reason the biggest products in the world are entertainment and social.
zh: 世界上最大的产品是娱乐和社交，这是有原因的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, we get at the heart of how do we deliver the value to the consumer?
zh: 所以我们要触及核心问题：我们如何向消费者交付价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for most consumers, sometimes I tease and I say it's like the Instagram AI user versus the X AI user.
zh: 我想对大多数消费者来说——有时候我会调侃说，这就像 Instagram 的 AI 用户对比 X 的 AI 用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: The X AI user is fearful of being outside of the permanent underclass, is really opinionated on GLM-5.3 versus Kimi K3.
zh: X 的 AI 用户害怕自己被甩出那个永久底层，对 GLM-5.3 对比 Kimi K3 有着非常强烈的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just so pilled.
zh: 他们就是被彻底洗脑了(pilled)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the Instagram person is like, "Oh, this is like a better Google search.
zh: 而 Instagram 那个人就像：「哦，这就像一个更好用的 Google 搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of.
zh: 算是吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's cool."
zh: 挺酷的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't get what all the hype is about.
zh: 他们不明白这有什么好炒作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really a product design failure.
zh: 而这真的是一个产品设计上的失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have the capabilities to radically transform people's lives.
zh: 我们有能力从根本上改变人们的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Lenny, in many ways we spent 40 years building a technology that enables better spreadsheets.
zh: 我是说，Lenny，在很多方面我们花了 40 年建造了一项让电子表格变得更好的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built this technology that extends our intellect, but nothing to extend our soul.
zh: 我们建造了这项延伸我们智力的技术，却没有任何东西延伸我们的灵魂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that we have a little bit of a spiritual hunger, especially as a lot of these cultural institutions have gone away that fulfilled that, especially in the rest of America where you don't have as many hot yoga classes, and Pilates, and fasting, and Friendsgiving.
zh: 而且我觉得我们有一种精神上的饥渴，尤其是当许多曾经满足这种需求的文化机构消失之后，尤其是在美国其他地方，那里没有那么多热瑜伽课、普拉提、断食和 Friendsgiving。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that the opportunity for this technology is like, hey, the basics of consumer need, how do we feel more connected, more loved?
zh: 所以，我觉得这项技术的机会在于：嘿，消费者需求的基本面——我们如何感觉更连接、更被爱？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we make progress?
zh: 我们如何取得进步？ [[361A/381]] 我们如何玩得开心？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we have fun?
zh: 我们怎么找乐子?

speaker: Unknown
en: The things that we all aspire to, the basics, how do we apply this technology to those areas?
zh: 我们所有人向往的那些东西、那些基本的东西，我们如何把这项技术应用到那些领域？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I want to see more of.
zh: 这就是我想看到更多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I don't think it's a model or a capability challenge.
zh: 再说一次，我不认为这是一个模型或能力上的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a product design challenge.
zh: 它只是一个产品设计的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this so much.
zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about this idea of, "Loop, grow my business.
zh: 我们谈过「Loop，让我的生意增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Loop, find me more sales.
zh: Loop，帮我找到更多销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: Loop, close support tickets."
zh: Loop，关闭支持工单」这类想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the way you're describing here, I think you, the way I had it in my notes here, just like, "Loop, improve my health," or, "Loop, make me a better friend."
zh: 但按你在这里描述的方式——我在笔记里就是这么写的——就像「Loop，改善我的健康」，或者「Loop，让我成为更好的朋友」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's no reason AI can't just think deeply and hard about all those things and figure out a way to actually do this.
zh: 而且没有理由 AI 不能就这些事情深入而认真地思考，并想出真正做到这些的办法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, look, we have to dial this in, but I think there's a way that AI can challenge you, can push you, can be disagreeable.
zh: 而且还有，你看，我们得把这个调校好，但我认为 AI 有一种方式可以挑战你、可以推动你、可以跟你唱反调。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is also why I think startups are advantaged over incumbents.
zh: 这也是为什么我认为创业公司相比现有巨头更有优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea those 1,000 Google committees who would roll in their graves at the idea that they're going to release a model that's disagreeable, or God forbid it should be sexually suggestive, but guess what?
zh: 那一千个 Google 委员会，一想到要发布一个会唱反调的模型——更别提它居然还应该带点性暗示——就会从坟墓里气得打滚，但你猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are all parts of human existence.
zh: 这些全都是人类生存体验的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think exploring the kind of uncomfortable parts of our social existence are things that startups are uniquely set up to do.
zh: 所以，我觉得探索我们社会存在中那些令人不舒服的部分，是创业公司 uniquely 具备条件去做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know you spent a lot of time investing in consumer companies.
zh: 而且我知道你花了很多时间投资消费类公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm hearing here is this is a big opportunity for consumer businesses to basically build an app product that is exactly this loop around improve my connections with my friends and family.
zh: 我在这里听到的是，这对消费类业务来说是一个巨大的机会——基本上就是构建一个完全围绕这个循环的应用产品：改善我和朋友及家人的连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's right.
zh: 我觉得没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the thing that's held back consumer so far a little bit, and it maybe held back is too strong, because if we put this into iPhone terms, we're in iPhone 2010.
zh: 我认为到目前为止稍微拖累消费级产品的东西——说“拖累”也许太重了，因为如果用 iPhone 的说法来讲，我们现在处于 iPhone 2010 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is iPhone 2010?
zh: 什么是 iPhone 2010 年？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's pre-Airbnb, pre-WhatsApp, pre-Uber, pre all the important consumer companies.
zh: 我觉得那是 Airbnb 之前、WhatsApp 之前、Uber 之前、所有重要消费级公司诞生之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it is early days, but what's held us back is I think three things.
zh: 所以现在还很早，但我认为拖住我们的有三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is that the models have been expensive, so if you want to do a kind of free to use product, that hasn't been easy.
zh: 一是模型一直很贵，所以如果你想做一个免费使用的产品，那并不容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is that we've had an interface problem.
zh: 第二是我们一直有界面问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chat makes sense if you're the highest agency person in the world, which is Elon and Sam, but for the average consumer, their ideal interface is TikTok.
zh: 如果你 是世界上主观能动性最高的人——也就是 Elon 和 Sam——聊天界面说得通，但对普通消费者来说，他们理想的界面是 TikTok。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, we need to find something between Chat and TikTok.
zh: →(上面已译)

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the fact that the technology has been so much more focused on productivity than things like human connection and entertainment, I think all those things are kind of up for grabs.
zh: 然后是这项技术一直过于聚焦生产力，而不是像人际连接和娱乐这类东西，我认为这些领域都还有很大机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: The open weight models mean things are way cheaper.
zh: 开放权重模型意味着成本大大降低。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that we're starting to have conversations about things like, "Loop, make me happier."
zh: 我认为我们开始有这样的对话了，比如：“Loop，让我更快乐。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that founders like Eugenia, who you should have on the show, she's tremendous, are thinking really ambitiously about user interfaces.
zh: 而且我认为像 Eugenia 这样的创始人——你应该请她上节目，她非常出色——正在以非常有雄心的方式思考用户界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brian Chesky from Airbnb, I think he started a foundation lab focused on next gen user interfaces.
zh: Airbnb 的 Brian Chesky，我记得他创办了一个专注于下一代用户界面的实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think all those problems will get solved or they're at least in a better position to be solved than they were two years ago.
zh: 所以，我认为所有这些问题都会被解决，或者说至少比两年前处于更有利的位置被解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to come back to the whole space of consumer and AI and things like that, but I want to follow this thread a little bit more about just the optimism around where things might go.
zh: 我想回到消费级和 AI 以及相关领域的整体话题，但我想再多追问一点关于事物可能走向何方的乐观情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of fear and worry about the future with AI and just generally.
zh: 人们对 AI 的未来有很多恐惧和担忧，总的来说也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark Andreessen when he came on the pod had this really interesting take that AI came just in time to save us, because population is declining, productivity's going down, there's all this war, climate change and all these things, and we would be in big trouble if AI wasn't here to fill that gap.
zh: Mark Andreessen 上播客时有一个非常有意思的观点：AI 来得恰到好处，刚好及时拯救了我们，因为人口在下降，生产力在下滑，还有战争、气候变化等等这一切，如果 AI 不在的话我们会陷入大麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just your bigger picture perspective on why you think maybe people are underestimating the positive and optimism around AI.
zh: 谈谈你更大的格局视角，为什么你认为人们可能低估了围绕 AI 的积极面和乐观情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, I think it's a potential for it to be a sort of emotional spiritual interface on which we can get leverage and explore aspects of ourselves that have been really buried.
zh: 第一，我认为它有潜力成为一种情感和精神的界面，我们可以借助它获得杠杆，探索我们自己身上一直被深深埋藏的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at the kind of effect of the industrial revolution, it's that there are these scale advantages which are insurmountable.
zh: 如果你看看工业革命的影响，那就是存在这些不可逾越的规模优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as much as obviously I'm very pro-capitalism and I love the economy that we live in, I think that centralization, it sort of discourages the individual in some ways and it maybe detracts from their identity.
zh: 尽管显然我非常支持资本主义，也热爱我们生活的这个经济体，但我认为中心化在某种程度上压制了个人，也许会削弱他们的身份认同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think one of the really magical things is this is a technology that really amplifies our identity, our agency, it kind of unbundles skill from desire.
zh: 所以，我认为最神奇的事情之一是，这是一项真正放大我们身份认同、我们的主观能动性的技术，它把技能和欲望解绑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, if you want to make music, you can make music now.
zh: 举例来说，如果你想制作音乐，你现在就可以制作音乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to know how to play the piano.
zh: 你不需要会弹钢琴。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to be a programmer and make software, you can make software now.
zh: 如果你想当程序员、做软件，你现在就可以做软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it really amplifies our individuality, it allows us to explore aspects of our lives that we were never able to explore before.
zh: 所以它真正放大了我们的个体性，让我们能够探索生命中以前从未能探索的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just in terms of the nuts and bolts, we have been in this sort of morass of 2% GDP growth.
zh: 而且单从基本层面来看，我们一直陷在 2% GDP 增长的泥潭里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who said that we have to be there?
zh: 谁说我们必须待在那里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't we be 10 or 15 or 20%?
zh: 为什么我们不能是 10%、15% 或 20%？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a technology with which not only can we dramatically drive productivity, we can dramatically drive ambition.
zh: 而且这是一项技术，不仅能极大地推动生产力，还能极大地推动雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe this is a caricature, but the 1950s and 1960s we believed that we could do anything.
zh: 也许这有点夸张，但在 1950 年代和 1960 年代，我们相信自己什么都能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were coming out of World War II where the entire economy, the entire world mobilized in a way that we didn't think was possible.
zh: 我们刚从二战中走出来，整个经济、整个世界以一种我们原以为不可能的方式被动员起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of my theories, Lenny, is that when the stakes are high we are awesome.

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a lot of ways, I think the world we lived in five years ago felt like a low stakes world, which is why we collectively had a lot of these side projects as a society which weren't necessarily productive or making any of us happier.

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you've got, it's not just Elon doing everything he's doing, but I think everybody feels like they're climbing the ambition ladder.
zh: 而现在，不只是 Elon 在做他做的所有事，我认为每个人都感觉自己正在攀登雄心的阶梯。

speaker: Unknown
en: You ship your bad ideas so you can discover your good ideas.
zh: 你先把糟糕的点子做出来，才能发现好的点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you want to build software, great.
zh: 如果你想做软件，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to build a bridge, you don't have to be a civil architect to know how to do that anymore.

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I really think that we have the makings of a sort of dramatically happier, more fulfilled, more productive society, and yet we're here talking about permanent underclass.
zh: 所以，我真的认为我们已经具备成为一个显著更快乐、更充实、更有生产力的社会的基础，然而我们却在这里谈论永久性的底层阶级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love all of that, that all feels so right.
zh: 我喜欢这一切，这一切感觉都太对了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so hard to really believe that.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但如果你真看看目前为止 AI 崛起以来事情的走向，失业率下降了，人们在赚很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously a lot of people are struggling, there's a lot of downsides, data centers causing problems for people, things like that.
zh: 显然很多人还在挣扎，有很多负面因素，数据中心给人们带来了问题，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of issues, but it feels like as an economy and as a country feels like things are going well so far.
zh: 有很多问题，但感觉上作为一个经济体、作为一个国家，目前为止事情进展得不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just almost cured some kind of cancer the other day.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我是说，Dario 能写一篇博客文章说“当我们治愈所有疾病时会发生什么”，这个事实本身就说明了一切。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think that we're collectively worried always, these abstractions, the world, the average worker, the middle manager, the person who lives in the vicinity of a data center, these are abstractions, but our actual lives seem like they're getting more fulfilled, we're more capable, we're more empowered.

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that's also something that the revealed preferences tend to show how people are experiencing it individually, and the stated preferences tend to show how people are sort of observing it or believe it's playing out societally.
zh: 所以,我认为这也是显示性偏好往往反映人们个体层面如何体验它,而陈述性偏好往往反映人们在观察它或相信它会如何在社会层面演进的方式。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 如果你问人们是否想在自家附近建数据中心,大多数人会说不要,但如果你问他们今天是否用了 ChatGPT,大多数人会说用了。

zh: 顺便说一句,还有把地位从文凭中拆分出来。你不需要哈佛学位,你只需要拿到——这很酷。

zh: 他们暂停了他们最新模型上的 RL 阶段,因为他们看到的情况。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以,这对人们来说显然是个大担忧——这些模型到底会变得多快、多聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any thoughts on just that?
zh: 对此有什么想法吗?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这现在是一个很大的转变。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 又或者他们当时 GPU 短缺。

zh: 现在,也许那些能力比他们实际想要的更先进。

zh: 也许他们其实想把那个专有模型留在内部,以延长他们自己的领先优势。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以,我认为有很多混杂的因素会导致你稍微往回收一收。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I do take the points about offensive cyber seriously, which is we should harden all of our systems before we make them trivial to penetrate.
zh: 听着，我确实认真对待关于进攻性网络的观点，也就是我们应该在系统变得容易被轻易攻破之前先加固所有系统。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但我认为，“模型太危险不能发布”这种概念，某种程度上混淆了营销、推理容量，以及经济层面的考量，比如你是想把你的竞争优势外部化，还是用它来让自己变得更强？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我有点不好意思谈论我的很多项目，因为它们看起来不够重要或不够有分量，但其中很多是通过执行或发布来学习，或者通过执行和发布获得满足感。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 当你审视一家初创公司时，你是怎么思考持久性和护城河的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because a lot of founders get that question.
zh: 因为很多创始人都被问到这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's getting that question.

zh: 嗯，我认为有两个重要的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is something that Jesse from Decagon said, which I love, and that is that moats are most often discovered, not designed.
zh: 一个是 Decagon 的 Jesse 说过的，我很喜欢，那就是护城河往往是被发现出来的，而不是设计出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really easy, I've done this as a founder, to get in your own head about, "Hey, I need a business plan that survives scrutiny from MBAs and VCs.
zh: 我觉得很容易——我自己作为创始人也这样做过——陷入自己的思维旋涡：“嘿，我需要一个能经得起 MBA 和 VC 审视的商业计划。

zh: 我必须对我的护城河是什么有一个非常精妙的想法。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And for that team, they just started shipping and it developed over time.
zh: 而对那个团队来说，他们就是开始发布产品，护城河随时间逐渐形成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another great example of this is Cursor.
zh: 另一个很好的例子是 Cursor。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were criticized a lot for not having a moat, but it turned out that initially being a high NPS DAU product was really good.
zh: 他们因为缺乏护城河而受到很多批评，但事实证明，最初作为一个高 NPS 的高日活产品是非常好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And over time they captured all the reasoning traces, they trained their own models, the Composer 1 2 models, and so on and so forth.

speaker: Unknown
en: We know how that story plays out.
zh: 我们知道那个故事的结局。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So on this moat idea, so say you're a founder and you're putting a pitch together, trying to pitch you or other VCs, what's the best way to talk about a moat?
zh: 那么回到护城河这个话题，假设你是一位创始人，正在准备一份路演稿，试图向你们或其他 VC 做推介，谈论护城河的最好方式是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just say, "We're going to discover it.
zh: 你能不能就说，“我们要去发现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not sure.
zh: 我们不确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody really knows yet"?
zh: 目前还没有人真正知道”？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that we would happily take a bet on a product that doesn't have a "moat" or durability story if it has a lot of momentum, a lot of craft, a lot of growing engagement.
zh: 我认为，如果一个产品有很多势头、很多匠心、很多不断增长的参与度，我们会很乐意押注一个没有“护城河”或持久性故事的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually a thing I've learned over the years, I used to be very worried about people stealing my idea, but I've learned that the big ideas are always supported by a dozen small ideas that are invisible.
zh: 这其实是我这些年来学到的一件事，我以前非常担心别人偷走我的想法，但我学到了，大的想法总是由十几个看不见的小想法支撑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if somebody replicates your big idea, they never see the small ideas that make the big idea work.
zh: 而且即使有人复制了你的大想法，他们也永远看不到让大想法成立的小想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I actually think that there's just something special in the water with certain products that make them incredibly successful despite extraordinary competition.
zh: 所以，我实际上认为，某些产品就是水里有某种特别的东西，让它们尽管面对极其激烈的竞争也能获得巨大的成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, look at Granola.
zh: 我是说，看看 Granola。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two years ago it was really criticized, and I don't know that they have a super strong durability story today, and yet it is beloved and dominant.
zh: 两年前它受到很多批评，我不知道他们今天是否有一个非常强的持久性故事，但它却广受喜爱并且占据主导地位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I listen to what the customers are saying more than what the business books say.
zh: 我更听从客户在说什么，而不是商业书籍在说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get a free year of Granola if you become a subscriber to Lenny's newsletter.
zh: 如果你成为 Lenny 时事通讯的订阅者，你可以获得一年免费的 Granola。

speaker: Unknown
en: I should do this more often when it's part of this product pass, lennysproductpass.com.
zh: 当它属于这个产品通行证的一部分时，我应该更经常这样做，lennysproductpass.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get a free year of all these amazing products, including Granola.
zh: 获得所有这些出色产品的一年免费使用权，包括 Granola。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just saw RAM put out a report of the fastest growing companies according to their data, and Granola is number two or three.
zh: 我刚看到 RAM 根据他们的数据发布了一份增长最快公司的报告，Granola 排在第二或第三。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a tremendous product.
zh: 它是一个非常出色的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: The craft is really high.
zh: 匠心程度真的很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about that a lot these days because there's so much, there's Cowork, there's ChatGPT Work, there's Cursor, there's Grok Bot, and it's crazy how quickly one can switch from one to the other.
zh: 我最近经常想这件事，因为有太多产品了，有 Cowork，有 ChatGPT Work，有 Cursor，有 Grok Bot，而且人们能多么快速地从一个切换到另一个，这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the underlying model is not that different.
zh: 而且底层模型并没有那么不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: All it really is, most of it is the harness/UX of the product.
zh: 说真的，大部分其实就是产品的 harness/UX。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to me, that tells you there's so much opportunity in the actual user experience being a moat, or at least giving you a lot of time to find something that is durable.
zh: 所以对我来说，这告诉你，在真正的用户体验上做文章成为护城河，或者至少给你大量时间去找到某种持久的东西，这里面有巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think for the people that are at the edge, they pay for all of them because they all have the respective areas of specialization.
zh: 而且我认为对于处在前沿的那些人来说，他们为所有这些产品付费，因为它们各自都有各自的专业领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: I know, I know.

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.

zh: Grok 也是。

en: Oh yeah, you're right.
