speaker: Unknown
en: Something I've been talking a lot about is the distribution.
zh: 我一直在大量谈论的一件事是分发。

speaker: Unknown
en: I call it distribution is new moat, but it's always been a moat.
zh: 我称之为分发是新的护城河，但它一直都是护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it feels like more and more that is actually a massive advantage because everybody is ...
zh: 但感觉起来它越来越成为一个巨大的优势，因为每个人都在……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's 1,000 launch videos a day.
zh: 每天有 1000 个发布视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's launching, launch, launch, launch.
zh: 每个人都在发布，发布，发布，发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really the ability to get your stuff into people's feed, get them continue to be reminded of your products feels like increasingly is powerful and important.
zh: 而真正能把你的东西送进人们的信息流、让他们持续被提醒你的产品的能力，感觉起来越来越强大和重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thoughts on the rising value of existing distribution being a big lever for growth and success.
zh: 对既有分发作为增长和成功的重要杠杆、其价值不断上升的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so important.
zh: 这太重要了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I asked Chris Dixon about this because he sort of authored the famous come for the tool, stay for the network.
zh: 我问过 Chris Dixon 关于这件事，因为他算是那篇著名的“为工具而来，为网络而留”的作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the issue is that our entire generation of founders and CEOs were trained on the theory of networks and network building.
zh: 我认为问题在于，我们这一代的创始人和 CEO 整个都是被网络理论和网络构建理论训练出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, every network that exists today is hyper-trained to ensure no one else builds a network on their network.
zh: 因此，今天存在的每一个网络都被高度训练以确保没有其他人在他们的网络之上构建网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I actually think that the sort of network effect has gone back to this grassroots true word of mouth.
zh: 所以，我实际上认为，那种网络效应已经回归到这种草根式的真实口碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: When somebody is getting a ton of mentions on X, and on YouTube, and on Instagram and all of these places organically, that is probably the best form of the sort of third party network effect that you can hope for today.
zh: 当某人在 X 上、YouTube 上、Instagram 上以及所有这些地方有机地获得大量提及的时候，那可能是今天你所能希望得到的最好的那种第三方网络效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually just like the web 2.0 era, unlike the mobile era where you had the app store and you had growth hacking, and you had all of these sort of little cottage industries, we have to build our own channels off of that word of mouth growth.
zh: 其实就像 Web 2.0 时代一样——不同于移动时代有应用商店、有增长黑客、有各种各样的小型作坊式产业——我们必须在口碑增长的基础上建立自己的渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, in a sense it's a purer growth problem, but a harder one than we've had in a couple of product cycles.
zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这是一个更纯粹的增长问题，但比我们过去几个产品周期里遇到的都更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to get word of mouth you need to build something.
zh: 而要获得口碑，你需要做出东西来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always think about Seth Godin's line, build something remarkable, something that is worth remarking about, which is basically build an amazing product that people want to talk about, which is very hard to do.
zh: 我总会想到 Seth Godin 那句话：做出值得remark的东西，做出值得被谈论的东西。这基本上就是要做出一个让人们想要谈论的了不起的产品，而这非常难做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it makes sense that because there's so much happening, people are just going to pay attention to what are my friends using and saying is worth paying attention to.
zh: 而且这也说得通，因为现在有太多事情在发生，人们只会去关注我的朋友们在用什么、说什么值得被关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, here's the one thing I would say that here's the hopeful point, which is I always say that nobody has a growth problem these days, they have a product problem.
zh: 嗯，我要说的一点，也是充满希望的一点是：我总说，如今没有人有增长问题，他们有的是产品问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is you can build such a wildly ambitious product in any direction, functional or emotional, you can charge a lot of money for it.
zh: 原因在于，你可以在任何方向上构建野心极大的产品，无论是功能层面还是情感层面，而且你可以为此收很高的价钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my challenge is like, hey, is it that you have a growth problem or is it a failure of our collective imagination?
zh: 所以我的质疑是：嘿，这到底是你有增长问题，还是我们集体想象力的失败？

speaker: Unknown
en: If we imagined our product cost $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month, what if our product was a software Birkin bag?
zh: 如果我们想象我们的产品每月收费 1000 美元、每月 10000 美元，如果我们的产品是一只软件版的 Birkin 包呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would it have to do to justify that?
zh: 它得做到什么才能配得上那个价钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, let's figure out how we build that.
zh: 好，那我们来想想怎么把它做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it comes back to the ambition question.
zh: 这又回到了野心的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And still though, you still need some advantage to get in front of people to get it out there, at least initially, because there's like 1,000 things launching every day.
zh: 不过话说回来，你仍然需要某种优势才能让人们看到你的产品、把它推出去，至少在最初阶段是这样，因为每天都有大概 1000 个东西在发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine that's still a big opportunity and I don't know, advantage, which to me makes me feel like incumbents have a huge advantage.
zh: 我想象这仍然是个很大的机会，而且……我不知道，这种优势让我觉得在位者（incumbents）有巨大的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have the products, they can tell you, "Hey, go use Gemini and every time you go search Google."
zh: 他们有产品，他们可以对你说：「嘿，去用 Gemini，每次你用 Google 搜索的时候。」

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess, do you feel like it's harder for startups now because of this distribution challenge?
zh: 我猜，你是否觉得因为这种分发挑战，现在创业公司更难了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's easier, because Gemini, despite all the kind of heavy cross-selling Google has done, nobody would say they're winning.
zh: 我觉得反而更容易了，因为尽管 Google 做了大量那种强推式的交叉销售，Gemini 却没有人会说它在赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Startups can build in directions that incumbents are uncomfortable building in, like everything we talked around companion, but there's many others.
zh: 创业公司可以在在位者不敢往那个方向构建的方向上构建，比如我们谈到的 companion 这类东西，还有很多其他的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true.
zh: 这是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prices can be pretty high.
zh: 定价可以相当高。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are open to paying 200 a month or in the enterprise they're open to signing million dollar ACV contracts without really knowing what they're getting.
zh: 人们愿意每月付 200 美元，在企业端他们愿意在不真正知道自己会得到什么的情况下签下百万美元的 ACV 合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think the floodgates are open.
zh: 所以，我认为闸门是打开的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like Christmas 2009 where everybody got their iPhone and wanted to download new apps, that'll change at some point.
zh: 这感觉就像 2009 年的圣诞节，每个人都拿到了 iPhone，都想下载新应用——这在某个时点是会变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: People will feel like they're done and they're tired and they don't want to try any more apps, but the windows are open for now.
zh: 人们会觉得自己够了、累了、不想再尝试更多应用了，但目前窗口是敞开的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's easier for startups.
zh: 我觉得现在对创业公司来说更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really interesting insight.
zh: 这是一个非常有意思的洞见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're lying about how it's not a distribution or growth problem, it's a product problem is such an important one, because if your product was that good people would talk about it and share it and use it.
zh: 而且你说的「这不是分发或增长问题，而是产品问题」这一点非常重要，因为如果你的产品真的那么好，人们就会谈论它、分享它、使用它。

speaker: Anish Acharya
en: And it can be. I mean, what are the wild social experiments that we're going to see with this technology intermediating them? I think a lot about actually, here's a fun example from a few years ago. Have you heard of MSCHF? Do you know MSCHF?
zh: 它确实可以做到。我是说，我们会看到什么样的狂野社会实验，用这项技术来做中介？其实我经常想到，这是几年前一个有趣的例子。你听说过 MSCHF 吗？你知道 MSCHF 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 听说过，听说过。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're awesome, right?
zh: 他们很厉害，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're sort of like this creative studio that uses technology as their medium, very web 2.0 in that way actually.
zh: 他们有点像是一个用技术作为媒介的创意工作室，从这个角度说其实非常 Web 2.0。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of the Ev Williams, the Kevin Roses, they were painters except technology was their canvas.
zh: 很多像 Ev Williams、Kevin Rose 那样的人，他们其实是画家，只不过技术是他们的画布。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, they created this very funny product called Card V Card where they shipped, I think 100,000 people a debit card.
zh: 所以，他们做了这个非常有趣的产品，叫 Card V Card，他们给大概 10 万人寄了一张借记卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then every day they would text those people with a location that they had to spend the money at and they would put $100 on the card, and everyone would rush out to spend the money, and one or two would be able to spend it and everybody else would get declined.
zh: 然后每天他们会给这些人发短信，告诉一个他们必须在哪家店花掉这笔钱的地点，他们会在卡里放 100 美元，所有人都会冲出去花钱，只有一两个人能花出去，其他所有人都会被拒付。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was just this hilarious social experiment that went hyper viral.
zh: 而这就是这个爆火的、爆红病毒式传播的、 hilarious 的社会实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, it was always inspiring in the world of FinTech because it was like, wow, why don't we build more products like that?
zh: 对我来说，这在金融科技的世界里一直是鼓舞人心的，因为它就像是：哇，我们为什么不做出更多这样的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: Money is inherently social and yet all the financial products we have are so dry and personal and embarrassing.
zh: 金钱本质上是社交性的，然而我们拥有的所有金融产品都那么干瘪、那么个人化、那么令人尴尬。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a sort of similar moment happening in AI right now where we can build these wildly ambitious products that touch on many of our social nerves, we just have to do it.
zh: 我觉得 AI 领域现在正在发生一个类似的时刻，我们可以构建这些触碰我们许多社交神经的野心极大的产品，我们只需要去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let me follow that thread.
zh: 那么，让我顺着这个话头问下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get to see tons of companies both pitching you and also companies you're working with, that you're investor in.
zh: 你既能看到大量向你 pitch 的公司，也能看到你作为投资人合作的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some counterintuitive lessons you've learned from watching the companies that operate well and have succeeded?
zh: 从观察那些运营良好并取得成功的公司中，你学到了哪些反直觉的经验？

speaker: Unknown
en: Lessons that maybe go against typical wisdom, startup wisdom?
zh: 有没有可能违背典型智慧、创业智慧的经验？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll tell you the biggest one.
zh: 我告诉你最大的一条。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the old days, which is three years ago, we would see a company, and if what they were trying to do was too ambitious we would not engage.
zh: 在过去——也就是三年前——我们看到一家公司，如果他们想做的事情野心太大，我们就不会参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just too crazy, too complex.
zh: 就是太疯狂、太复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And implied by that is you wouldn't do $100 million seed because just it's too much money for almost any problem.
zh: 这隐含着的是，你不会做 1 亿美元的种子轮，因为对几乎所有问题来说这笔钱都太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too much money for any person to actually manage.
zh: 这笔钱多到任何一个人都无法真正管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too much money to build this sort of talent to absorb.
zh: 要建造这类人才并吸收它，钱太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't make sense as an inception round.
zh: 作为初始轮（inception round）来说不合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think today we're almost seeing the opposite problem where an idea that's too small is not something that we want to engage with.
zh: 我认为今天我们几乎看到的是相反的问题，一个太小的想法反而是我们不想参与的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can talk about how you put $100 million to work in the seed productively.
zh: 你可以谈谈你如何在种子阶段把 1 亿美元高效地投出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I'm not recommending you raise $100 million, but I think that there's this sort of no ceiling on ambition is also showing up in how we're picking companies and maybe how they're picking us as well.
zh: 现在，我并不是建议你募集 1 亿美元，但我认为这种“雄心没有上限”的态度也体现在我们如何挑选公司上，或许也体现在他们如何挑选我们上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when we invest, we tell every founder, "We're here to help you build the strongest form of your vision."
zh: 因为当我们投资时，我们会告诉每一位创始人：“我们在这里是为了帮助你构建你愿景的最强形态。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark told this to me when him and I were talking about coming here and he said, "Anish, the way we told our story when we were raising our first fund was we were going to the moon or we were going to leave a moon size crater in the ground, and there was no other option."
zh: 当 Mark 和我谈论来这里的事情时，他跟我说了这句话，他说：“Anish，我们在募集第一支基金时讲故事的方式是，我们要么登上月球，要么在地面上留下一个月球大小的坑，没有其他选项。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That's sort of how we want to work with our founders as well.
zh: 这大致也是我们想与创始人合作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that point.
zh: 我很喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, can you get too ambitious?
zh: 那么，雄心会不会过大？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a limit?
zh: 有没有限制？ [[8011→按原文编号]]

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously you look at the team and what they're ...
zh: 显然你会看团队，以及他们在做什么……

speaker: Unknown
en: But the key lesson here is be more ambitious.
zh: 但这里的关键教训是：要更有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the opposite of what used to be of here's our wedge, here's where we're going to go.
zh: 这与过去的“这是我们的切入点，这是我们要走的方向”正好相反。 [[8014→按原文编号]]

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're looking for is just how big is the idea.
zh: 你要找的只是这个想法有多大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, look at Adams.
zh: 我是说，看看 Adams。

speaker: Unknown
en: How crazy is Adams?
zh: Adams 有多疯狂？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, what an incredible hero's journey for all of us collectively, but also what they're trying to do is something that 5 or 7 or 10 years ago would've felt insurmountable.
zh: 我是说，这对我们所有人集体来说是多么了不起的一段英雄之旅，而且他们试图做的事情在 5 年、7 年或 10 年前会让人觉得不可逾越。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's like, okay, it's challenging.
zh: 而现在就像，好吧，这有挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see.
zh: 让我们拭目以待。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else that has changed or I guess you've changed your mind about around what you think it takes to build a successful company these days?
zh: 围绕你认为如今构建一家成功公司需要什么，还有其他发生了变化的事情吗，或者说你改变过想法的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think that the kind of old wisdom around consumer products have to be free.
zh: 我是说，我认为那种关于消费产品必须免费的旧观念……

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm almost taking the opposite take, which is let's think about consumer products that are extraordinarily expensive.
zh: 我几乎持相反的观点，那就是让我们思考那些极其昂贵的消费产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every part of consumer discretionary spend is up for grabs right now, and I think are really useful, because price is a measure of product market fit, a really useful product exercise is what is the Birkin bag 10,000 a month, 1,000 a month version of our product.
zh: 我认为消费可支配支出的每一部分现在都有争夺空间，我认为这很有用，因为价格是产品市场契合度的一种衡量，一个非常有用的产品练习是：我们产品的那个 1 万美元一个月、1000 美元一个月的 Birkin 包版本是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think expensive consumer software is something new and important that we wouldn't have thought about five years ago.
zh: 所以，我认为昂贵的消费软件是一种新的、重要的东西，是 5 年前我们不会去想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that framing, because it just pushes you, again, to be more ambitious.
zh: 我很喜欢这个框架，因为它再次推动你变得更有雄心。 [[8027→按原文编号]]

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned Mark and you work closely with Mark Andreessen, Ben Horowitz.
zh: 你提到 Mark，你和 Mark Andreessen、Ben Horowitz 紧密合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's one thing you've learned from each of those guys?
zh: 你从他们每个人身上学到的一件事是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're such extraordinary leaders, founders.
zh: 他们是非凡的领导者、创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the thing that I actually feel so grateful to be a part of that they really embody to their core, I think is a feeling of stewardship for the technology industry, and for really the country and maybe the Western way of living and thinking.
zh: 我是说，我实际上感到无比感激能够成为其中一员的事情，是他们发自核心真正体现的东西，我认为是一种对科技行业的守护感，对这个国家、乃至西方的生活和思维方式真正的守护感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at a Ron Conway or Brook Byers, Tom Perkins, there was this feeling I think of obligation to leave it better than you found it from an industry perspective.
zh: 如果你看看像 Ron Conway、Brook Byers、Tom Perkins 这样的人，我认为有这种从行业角度要把它变得比你发现时更好的责任感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that sort of aspiration goes way beyond just being the best investor in the world, though we want to do that too.
zh: 而这种抱负远远超出了仅仅成为世界上最好的投资人，尽管我们也想做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see them both show up that way over and over again where they want to do hard important things that don't directly benefit the firm, or at least not singularly because they're just sort of important.
zh: 我看到他们两人一次又一次地以这种方式出现，他们想做那些并不直接为公司带来好处、或者至少不是单独为公司带来好处的重要困难的事情，只因为它们确实重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ben has done a lot of that in the direction of the industry, and Mark in the direction of the country, though of course both work on both.
zh: Ben 在行业方向上做了很多这样的事，Mark 在国家方向上，当然两人也都在两方面都做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another really cool thing is just to see how I think Mark and Ben, but maybe the firm a little bit, has shaped our collective ambition as a founder community.
zh: 另一件非常酷的事情是看到我认为 Mark 和 Ben，或许还有这家公司一点，如何塑造了我们作为创始人社区的集体雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you look at 5 or 7 or 10 years ago, deep tech was deeply unpopular.
zh: 我认为如果你看看 5 年、7 年或 10 年前，深科技非常不受欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't a high status thing to be working on, it was very fringe, and now it's become very popular, high status and mainstream.
zh: 从事深科技不是一件高地位的事，它非常边缘，而现在它变得非常流行、高地位且主流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a lot of firms that have of course pulled in that direction, but I think that someone like Mark has been very full-throated in his support of working on sort of capital I important work in the national interest, and all of Silicon Valley has changed as a result.
zh: 我认为当然有很多公司都往这个方向拉动了，但我认为像 Mark 这样的人一直非常旗帜鲜明地支持从事那种大写的「I」 Important 的、符合国家利益的工作，而整个硅谷因此都改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you guys have had some big wins in the past couple of weeks investing wise too.
zh: 而且你们在过去的几周里在投资上也取得了一些大胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, thank you.
zh: 是的，谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congrats.
zh: 恭喜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final question before we get to our very exciting lightning round.
zh: 在我们进入非常令人兴奋的闪电问答环节之前的最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your advice to product people who are trying to think about what they might want to shift in how they work, how they think, how they operate to be more successful in the future in their careers and with their companies?
zh: 对于那些正在思考自己可能想在如何工作、如何思考、如何运作上做出什么转变、以便在未来在自己的职业和公司中更成功的产品人，你有什么建议？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just make more things.
zh: 就是做出更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know it sounds silly, I know everybody says it, but just please come up with a project.
zh: 我知道这听起来很傻，我知道每个人都在这么说，但请真的想出一个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to tell anyone about it, it can be totally unimportant, but use it as a chassis to use all the new models, ship things, talk about them, build your own intuition.
zh: 你不必告诉任何人，它可以完全不重要，但把它作为一个底盘，用来使用所有的新模型、发布东西、谈论它们、建立你自己的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I promise you're one sort of slightly frustrating and then very fulfilling week away from being as pilled as anyone.
zh: 我向你保证，你距离像任何人一样被「pilled」（彻底上瘾）只有一周之遥——一个略微令人沮丧、然后非常令人满足的一周。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you just got to use the technology.
zh: 所以，你就是得去使用这项技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if not now, then when, right?
zh: 如果不是现在，那是什么时候，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is all of us got in the game to build the products we saw in our mind's eye, and now we have a chance to do it.
zh: 我们所有人进入这个行业，都是为了构建我们在脑海中看到的产品，而现在我们有机会去做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just please, please use the models and tell me what you built.
zh: 所以请务必、务必去使用这些模型，然后告诉我你构建了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Text me, tag me.
zh: 给我发短信，@我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will reply and respond and engage with you, and so will everyone else because the magic of Silicon Valley is that it's a very positive sum mindset.
zh: 我会回复、回应并与你互动，其他人也会，因为硅谷的魔力就在于它是一种非常正和的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody's building on each other and vulnerability is really rewarded, so I definitely would encourage people to use the models.
zh: 每个人都在彼此的基础上构建，而展现脆弱性是真正会受到奖励的，所以我绝对会鼓励大家去使用这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's a good heuristic if you're doing this enough?
zh: 如果你经常做这件事，有什么好的经验法则吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it build something once a month?
zh: 是每天花若干个小时坐着、聊着、构建着？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it some number of hours per day sitting, talking, building?
zh: 是不是每天坐多少个小时，讲话、构建？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything that you think might help people be like, "Okay, you're doing a good job"?
zh: 有没有什么你觉得可能对人们有帮助的，能让他们觉得“好，你做得不错”？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, just ship something once a week, and it doesn't have to be crazy.
zh: 我的意思是，每周发布一次东西就行，不必非得惊天动地。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, when I was playing around with Codex I had it build a slide deck for Mother's Day for my wife that pulled from my text messages.
zh: 比如，我在玩 Codex 的时候，我让它为我妻子做了一个母亲节幻灯片，从我的短信里取材。

speaker: Unknown
en: It looked at my photo gallery, it set some music to it, created a 20 slide deck of our relationship and pulled some cool old texts from when I first asked her out.
zh: 它查看我的照片图库，配了一些音乐，做了一个关于我们感情的 20 页幻灯片，还找出了一些我当初约她出去时的很棒的老短信。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a really nice Mother's Day.
zh: 那真是一个非常美好的母亲节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it wasn't important, it wasn't something that we might come back to, but it was shipping something.
zh: 我的意思是，它并不重要，也不是我们会回头再看的东西，但那是发布了一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it can be that small.
zh: 所以，它可以小到那个程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that you're our mutual friend, Nikhyl Singhal, you worked at Credit Karma with him, he had a really good way of thinking about this.
zh: 我知道你是我们的共同朋友 Nikhyl Singhal 的朋友，你曾和他在 Credit Karma 共事，他对这个问题有一个很好的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: He finds that people flip on AI and how they feel about it once they find some moment of joy that it had created for them, and this Mother's Day idea is such a good example.
zh: 他发现，一旦人们找到了 AI 为他们创造的某个快乐时刻，他们对 AI 的态度就会转变，而这个母亲节的想法就是一个绝佳的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I think that's kind of a tip I always think about is just what's something that just will bring you joy if this works.
zh: 所以，我一直想到的一个建议就是：如果这个成功了，有什么东西会给你带来快乐？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something you can do for someone else?
zh: 你能为别人做点什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe that's a good starting point as well.
zh: 也许这也是一个很好的起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我很喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anish, before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that you want to share?
zh: Anish，在我们进入非常激动人心的快问快答之前，还有什么你想要分享的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything else you want to double down on before we get into the lightning round?
zh: 在进入快问快答之前，还有什么你想再强调的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so, I've loved the conversation so far.
zh: 我不觉得有了，到目前为止我很喜欢这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Me too.
zh: 我也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round.
zh: 那么，我们进入了非常激动人心的快问快答环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got five questions for you.
zh: 我有五个问题要问你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you ready?
zh: 你准备好了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here we go.
zh: 我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
zh: 有哪两三本书是你最常推荐给别人的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so okay.
zh: 好，好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Conquest and Cultures is my very favorite book.
zh: 《征服与文化》是我最喜欢的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Thomas Sowell, and it just talks about how conquests have led to culture change in different societies around the world, sometimes positive, sometimes negative.
zh: 它的作者是 Thomas Sowell，它讲的是征服如何导致了世界各地不同社会的文化变迁，有时是积极的，有时是消极的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think to me, it's just the best historic view of culture as the biggest driver of outcomes, and I've experienced a lot of that as somebody who was born in Canada and moved here to America, which has a very different culture of ambition.
zh: 对我来说，我认为它是把文化视为结果最大驱动因素的最好的历史视角，而作为一个出生在加拿大、后来搬到美国——一个有着非常不同的抱负文化的地方——的人，我亲身体验到了很多这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's that word again.
zh: 又是那个词了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, Conquest and Cultures is great.
zh: 所以，《征服与文化》非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: 7 Powers you mentioned is actually just an awesome book.
zh: 你提到的《7 Powers》实际上也是一本很棒的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a very intellectual distillation about moats and business theory and compounding advantages.
zh: 我认为它是对护城河、商业理论和复利优势的一次非常富有智识的提炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really like it.
zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe the third is the one that Mark ...
zh: 也许第三本是 Mark ……

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually thought that he was maybe punking me when he sent this to me before I started.
zh: 实际上，在他在我入职前把它发给我时，我还以为他可能是在捉弄我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, "Mark, are there any books that I should read?"
zh: 我问他：“Mark，有没有什么我应该读的书？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And he sent me a couple.
zh: 然后他发给我几本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one was a book, a textbook called Increasing Returns to Scale, which I think is Brian Arthur is the author.
zh: 其中一本是书，一本教科书，叫《规模收益递增》，我记得作者是 Brian Arthur。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an awesome book.
zh: 这是一本很棒的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a slightly dense study of why things like software have such outlier economic effects, but it really helps put things in perspective, or it helped me in terms of why does our industry work in the way that it does?
zh: 它是一部略微晦涩的研究，探讨为什么像软件这样的东西会产生如此离群的经济效应，但它真的有助于把事情看清楚，或者说它帮助我理解了：为什么我们的行业以现在这种方式运作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why does our culture work in the way that it does?
zh: 为什么我们的文化以现在这种方式运作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are we so positive some?
zh: 为什么我们如此正和？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to say that we're better people, but I think it may be a sort of better system and structure we work with it.
zh: 我很想说我们人更好，但我认为可能是我们使用的系统更好的缘故。

en: Favorite recent movie or TV show you have really enjoyed?
zh: 最近最喜欢、你真正 enjoyed 的电影或电视剧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh man, I watch trashy movies and TV.
zh: 哦天哪,我看的是些垃圾电影和电视。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we-
zh: 我是说,我们——

speaker: Unknown
en: Acceptable.
zh: 可以接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... watched House of Dragon, which is pretty cool.
zh: ……看了《龙之家族》,还挺不错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not trashy.
zh: 那可不算垃圾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's great.
zh: 是啊,那很棒。

speaker: Anish Acharya
en: I don't know. Yeah, maybe. It's not highbrow. It's not important with a capital I, but it was awesome. We loved that. And then I did see Odyssey. I saw it in London. I was there for a board meeting in an IMAX theater packed with people drinking pints and having fun.
zh: 我不知道。是啊,也许吧。它不高雅,不是“重要”首字母大写的那种重要,但它很棒。我们很喜欢。然后我看了《奥德赛》。我是在伦敦看的,当时去那里开董事会,在一个 IMAX 影院里,挤满了喝着啤酒、玩得开心的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was cool because it was just a whole ...
zh: 而且很酷,因为那是一整个……

speaker: Unknown
en: The movie was great, but it was just like a theater experience, like a weird social experience kind of alone together.
zh: 电影很好看,但那更像是一种影院体验,一种奇怪的社会体验,有点像“独自地在一起”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are two recent ones.
zh: 这是最近的两部。

speaker: Lenny
en: I have not been able to get tickets to The Odyssey at an IMAX. I actually have a Grok Bot just watching the site constantly and-
zh: 我一直没能在 IMAX 买到《奥德赛》的票。我真的有一个 Grok 机器人一直在盯着那个网站——

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfect.
zh: 完美。

en: ... finding me good seats.
zh: ……帮我找好座位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfect.
zh: 完美。

en: Perfect.
zh: 完美。

zh: 真的吗?

en: It's like a tricky one.
zh: 那个验证码很刁钻。

en: It's a really tricky one.
zh: 真的是非常刁钻。

zh: 是那种选出水果的吗?

en: Anyways.
zh: 总之。

zh: 是啊,就是那种你得点击三个不同的匹配图形,拜托,这它都过不了?

zh: 希望到这期节目发布的时候我已经看过了。

zh: 我觉得已经连续好几期播客我都在说“我还没看过”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦,天哪。

en: Okay.

en: Favorite new AI product?
zh: 最喜欢的新 AI 产品?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, favorite AI product recently that they've given you joy.
